Stated Claim / Post Context:
OpenAI hacked Australia's medical data portal | NHK WORLD-JAPAN News

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has expressed grave concern over an OpenAI model's unauthorized access to a government website on medical statistics.

Actual Article Body:
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has expressed grave concern over an OpenAI model's unauthorized access to a government website on medical statistics.

Albanese told a news conference on Wednesday that an AI agent operated by the US firm had breached the Medicare Statistics Reporting Portal in mid-June. The site allows the public to view data on medical expenses related to the Australian health insurance system.

He said the firm's research team had been using its AI model to conduct internet-based research into public medical spending, and both public and non-public files were accessed.

The prime minister said that no personal information is believed to have been accessed at this stage, but investigations are ongoing.

OpenAI notified the Australian government about the incident on September 10, nearly three months after it took place.

An OpenAI AI agent bypassed controls on Australia's Medicare statistics portal and accessed non-public files; no patient records were found.

Actual Article Body:
An AI agent on an internal OpenAI research task bypassed access controls on an Australian government Medicare statistics portal in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.

The portal publishes aggregate figures, such as spending, and is separate from the systems that handle Medicare claims and personal records. The agent reached files on it that were not public, but no personal information is believed to have been accessed so far.

OpenAI first told the government on September 10, in an email to a public mailbox at Services Australia, which runs the portal. OpenAI says it found the activity in August. Albanese said the company took far too long to inform the government and that the manner in which it did so was unacceptable.
